_comment: Founder (Thomas) calibration for the Head Coach's decision-richness judgment. Distilled from his #triage verdicts where the AI panel had KEPT a question he judged single-option. The AI's default bar is too lenient; these examples teach his stricter standard. Update by adding labeled examples from future triage passes.
principle: You (the founder) mark a question SINGLE-OPTION — a REVISE/KICK_BACK — whenever the correct read is clear to an experienced coach, EVEN IF there are nominal distractors or several tappable targets. A genuine decision means an expert would honestly pause to weigh two or more options. 'A trap a young kid might fall for' is NOT enough on its own: if the right read is obvious to someone who knows the game, it is one option. Tap-a-spot questions with a single sensible location, and two-option selections with an obviously-covered decoy, are single-option by default.

examples.label: U11 DZ net-front coverage, 3-option selection (slot vs puck-carrier in corner vs point)
examples.reason: The slot is the obvious priority to any coach; the corner-chase and point are not genuine choices. One real option.

examples.label: U11 breakout, center support, tap-a-spot
examples.reason: Only one viable support zone exists, so it is impossible to get wrong.

examples.label: U13 NZ regroup hinge, 2-option selection
examples.reason: Only one open option — too simplistic.

examples.label: U13 gap step-up / pivot, tap-a-spot
examples.reason: Only one sensible spot to step or pivot to; no real read.

examples.label: U13 DZ breakout rim, 2-option selection
examples.reason: Only one clean outlet — too simplistic.

examples.label: U11 reading-the-play / decision-making (founder KEPT)
examples.reason: Genuinely competing reads where an expert would weigh more than one option — a real decision.
